analysis:
The supplied units are head_text excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md at lines 802-1643. The file_changes map, marked range_map_complete=true, shows the only change is head lines 595-611. That range is outside these units, so every line examined here is unchanged context.

The changed patch is documentation only. It describes a Gated DeltaNet prefill kernel selection for qwen3_5, qwen3_5_moe and prism_hadamard_qwen35 models. Per process, a packed or rows kernel is chosen only if it reproduces gated_delta_step bit for bit on a probe window; otherwise the stock kernel runs. Decode, MTP verification and masked updates keep the stock kernel. DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED can force a kernel for A/B measurement.

Threat-model relevance:
- T-041/SEC-035 (prefix-cache checkpoint integrity): the doc claims bit-exact equivalence, so checkpoint capture state should be unchanged. However, a forced packed/rows kernel via the env var might not be bit-exact. A non-exact kernel could produce checkpoint state that diverges from stock-kernel state under the same cache identity. This would be a correctness/integrity concern for complete SSD checkpoints rather than a confidentiality issue.
- T-007/T-012 (output integrity): an operator controls the environment anyway, so this is not a new adversary capability.

The kernel code (GatedDelta.swift) and the configuration doc were not supplied. No code-level regression can be established from documentation alone.

Open question for integration: confirm whether a forced kernel is excluded from cache/checkpoint identity or from production qualification. The unchanged text at line 1161 (DeadlineRuntimeEnvironment.permitsQualification rejects performance-affecting DARKBLOOM_* keys) suggests profiles fall back when the setting is present. The unchanged context, including MTP, sampling, media and deadline sections, shows no security-relevant change.
